To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C1473 G polymorphism of the Tph2 (tryptophan hydroxyalse) gene in mice is associated with brain TPH2 activity and intermale aggression.

(1) the TPH2 C1473G variant is associated with increased brain TPH2 activity and increased aggression in male mice, and (2) the C1473 allele is associated with higher TPH2 activity in the mid‐brain and higher number of attacks in aggressive encounters between males.
the C1473 polymorphism in the mouse Tph2 gene is associated with increased TPH activity in midbrain and increased number of attacks in intermale aggression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association of the TPH2 activity and intermale aggression with the Tph2 C1473G genetic variant in mice.
the role of Tph2 gene and TPH activity in aggression.
the genetic background of aggressive behavior in mice and the role of the serotoninergic system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tph2 gene C1473G SNP is not a major factor influencing aggressiveness in the mouse strains studied, however, this polymorphism is associated with Tph2 activity.
the 1473G allele is associated with lower TPH activity, lower aggressiveness and lower serotonin levels in mice.
the 1473G allele of Tph2 is associated with a decrease in TPH activity, which is associated with a reduction of intermale aggression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C1473G is a genetic factor that influences the aggressiveness phenotype in the laboratory mice and it is a potential genetic marker for aggression in humans.
the 1473G allele in Tph2 is associated with a lower brain TPH activity, which is in turn associated with a lower aggression in male mice.
the C1473C allele in the Tph 2 gene is linked to increased brain TPH activity, and this, in turn, is related to increased aggression.
The main takeaway from our work is that

genetic polymorphisms can be used as a tool for the selection of animal lines with different levels of aggression, and the results of our work can be used in the selection of animal models for the studies of aggression.
